Abscess: Infrequent complication of mastitis which can be caused by untreated mastitis, or delayed 
or ineffective treatment, failure to drain the mastic breast, or acute weaning during mastitis.
•• Confirm the presence of an abscess by ultrasound, needle aspiration incision.
•• Drainage should be considered.
•• Advise patients to continue breastfeeding since weaning or inhibiting lactation during treatment 
may hinder the rapid resolution of the abscess.

ing. Teaching should be initiated regarding proper positioning of the infant at the 
breast and proper latch-on. Instruction designed to teach the correct breastfeeding 
mechanics is the best prevention for nipple pain. The primary cause of sore nipples is 
thought to originate from faulty breastfeeding mechanics, that is, poor positioning, 
disorganized or dysfunctional sucking, improper latch-on, or failure to form a teat 
(the ability of the infant to draw the nipple and part of the areola deep into the mouth). 
Nurse Practitioners can readily manage most of the common problems associated 
with breastfeeding; however, referral to a mother-to-mother support group or a certi-
fied lactation consultant may be indicated.14,139
